source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 6ης Μαΐου — «Άγιοι Δάναξ, Μέσιρος και Θερίνος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 6 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and heads him first among the three, «Αγιος Θερινος». A company the page enumerates is one folder per member. **The page prints two forms of his name in one sentence** — «Θερίνος (ή Θηριανός)» — and only the head-line form is stored, with the alternative quoted in the name's note; nothing is transliterated and no third form is invented. **There is a Θερινός on saint.gr's 23 Απριλίου too, and this reader takes them for two men.** That entry is «Άγιοι Δονάτος και Θερινός οι Μάρτυρες», a pair perfected by the sword, drafted for that day as `therinus`; this one is a trio with Danax and Mesiros whose memory was kept at the Deuteron. Four things printed on the two pages separate them — a different company, a different martyrion, a different accent (Θερινός against Θερίνος), and the alternative form Θηριανός which only this page gives — and nothing on either page joins them; the sword is the one thing they share, and it is the commonest death in the book. **The 23 Απριλίου pair also carries a Δονάτος**, and this day carries a separate `donatus-6-may` who died by arrows and not by the sword, so the two pairs do not fold into one either. If a later reader decides otherwise, `therinos` and `therinus` are the two to fold, and neither was written as a row on a folder that would then have to be unpicked. **Δάναξ of this trio is not drafted here**: the corpus's `danax` already has a `venerated` Greek row on 16 Ιανουαρίου and is not a reader's to move, and whether he and this Danax are one man is left as a question in the report. **No year, no place, no emperor, no hymn**: the three were perfected by the sword and their memory was kept at their martyrion «εν τω Δευτέρω».
